newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen weaken on Sumitomo jitters.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen weaken on Sumitomo jitters.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) and Euroyen futures drifted lower on Wednesday after trade in a Japanese trust bank's stocks were suspended early in Tokyo.
Dealers said the market was unnerved by rumours that Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co had racked up foreign exchange losses and could be halting its international operations.
These were later denied by the company at a press briefing but cast more doubt on the stability of Japan's financial institutions, dealers said.
"The feature of the day was possibly big forex losses which pressured bonds and Euroyen," a dealer with a local bank said.
June JGBs settled at 123.73 against their previous 124.12.
Losses in JGBs were also attributed to position-squaring and rolling over of contracts ahead of the June contract expiry.
In Euroyen, confidence to buy was also dented by the Sumitomo rumours but dealers said speculative demand should resume as the market was technically supported.
"December is well bid at 98.90 and there's momentum to make a 99.05 top in the short-term," one Japanese commission house dealer said, shrugging off a potential hike in interest rates.

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday he expects the Bank of Japan not to change its monetary policy for a while as it has taken appropriate actions while keeping a careful watch on domestic and foreign situations.
The lead December Euroyen contract stood at 98.92 at 1115 GMT after hitting a high of 98.96 against an IMM close at 98.93.
Eurodollar futures experienced a lacklustre Asian session with investors wary of U.S. economic indicators this week.
Dealers said the European market, however, showed more interest with bids improving over the earlier part of the day.
